Common.name: Aether, the Empowering Dragon
Common.desc: When this card is Pendulum Summoned: You can target 1 card on the field; return it to the hand. You can only use this effect of "Aether, the Empowering Dragon" once per turn.

Common.name: Bashing Shield
Common.desc: Equip only to a Normal Summoned/Set monster. It gains 1000 ATK. You take no battle damage from attacks involving it.

Common.name: Battleguard King
Common.desc: Once per turn: You can Tribute any number of Warrior-Type monsters, except this card; for each Tributed monster, this card gains 1 additional attack during each Battle Phase this turn.

Common.name: Blue Dragon Summoner
Common.desc: If this card is sent from the field to the GY: You can add 1 Dragon, Warrior, or Spellcaster Normal Monster from your Deck to your hand.

Common.name: Dark Hole
Common.desc: Destroy all monsters on the field.

Common.name: Defense Draw
Common.desc: During your opponent's turn, at damage calculation: Make the battle damage you take from this battle 0, and if you do, draw 1 card.

Common.name: Doomstar Magician
Common.desc: Once per turn: You can discard 1 card, then target 1 card in either player's Pendulum Zone; destroy that card, and if you do, draw 1 card.

Common.name: Dragon Horn Hunter
Common.desc:
[ Pendulum Effect ] 
All Normal Monsters gain 200 ATK. You take no battle damage from battles involving Normal Monsters you control.

[ Monster Effect ] 
''The horns were needed to prepare a medicine for her village, suffering from a plague. Unknown to her, the dragons burned and trampled her village, once displaced from their den.''

Common.name: Dragoons of Draconia
Common.desc:
[ Pendulum Effect ] 
Once per turn, if a Normal Monster you control destroys an opponent's monster by battle, after damage calculation: You can add 1 Level 4 or higher Normal Monster from your Deck to your hand.

[ Monster Effect ] 
''Armed with muskets and iron spears, these mounted land troops of the Draconia Empire are feared by the Reptier Kingdom and other bordering nations.''

Common.name: Flash Knight
Common.desc: ''The power of the pendulum flashes forth from this shining knight.''

Common.name: Foucault's Cannon
Common.desc:
[ Pendulum Effect ] 
Once per turn, during the End Phase, if this card was activated this turn: You can target 1 face-up Spell/Trap Card on the field; destroy it.

[ Monster Effect ] 
''A mechanized life form, roving through space-time. But the mysterious thing is that its memory i... m...stly gone. W...at is t...e reason? D..... refuse t... b.... interfered w...h?''

Common.name: Inspiration
Common.desc: Target 1 face-up monster you control; it gains 700 ATK until the end of this turn.

Common.name: Lancephorhynchus
Common.desc:
[ Pendulum Effect ] 
If a Normal Monster you control attacks a Defense Position monster, inflict piercing battle damage to your opponent.

[ Monster Effect ] 
''This primordial species survived extinction by evolving an offensive lance that can pierce anything, although its diet still consists mainly of fish.''

Common.name: Mirror Force
Common.desc: When an opponent's monster declares an attack: Destroy all your opponent's Attack Position monsters.

Common.name: Mystical Elf
Common.desc: A delicate elf that lacks offense, but has a terrific defense backed by mystical power.

Common.name: Nightmare's Steelcage
Common.desc: This card remains on the field for 2 of your opponent's turns. While this card is face-up on the field, no monsters can attack.

Common.name: Old Vindictive Magician
Common.desc: FLIP: Target 1 monster your opponent controls; destroy that target.

Common.name: Reckless Greed
Common.desc: Draw 2 cards and skip your next 2 Draw Phases.

Common.name: Riryoku
Common.desc: Target 2 face-up monsters on the field; halve the ATK of 1 monster, and if you do, add that lost ATK to the other monster. These effects last until the end of this turn.

Common.name: Wonder Wand
Common.desc: Equip only to a Spellcaster monster. It gains 500 ATK. If you control the equipped monster and this card: You can send both to the GY; draw 2 cards.
